title: React Streaming UI That Delights
objective: After this lesson you will be able to parse SSE frames into typed UI states, preserve partials across reconnects with Last-Event-ID, render citations from parsed entities, and manage optimistic states with server reconciliation.
why: Streaming UX decides whether latency feels instant or broken: token-by-token rendering with citations beats spinners, resume preserves partials across drops, optimistic sends feel instant with server truth reconciling after. UI states are the product truth users see — API correctness without UI correctness ships broken experiences that pass all backend tests.

blocks.text: Parse SSE frames by contract version into **typed UI states**: streaming (partial tokens appending), citations (entities parsed on done-frames), error (envelope with retry action), complete (validated entity committed to state). Untyped string accumulation produces unrenderable blobs — frame contracts from Ch.1-2 make UI states exhaustive and testable.

blocks.caption: Exhaustive frame handling with forward tolerance built in

blocks.text: Drops reconnect with **Last-Event-ID**: server replays from the mark, client keeps rendered partials (no flash-of-empty), duplicates deduped by ID. Optimistic sends render instantly with pending flags; server truth reconciles (or rolls back with reason) on response. Restart-from-zero wastes money and patience; resume-everywhere is the discipline.

Done-frames carry validated entities: citations render as linked spans (source → chunk/page), prices with as-of dates, abstentions as designed empty states (gap + path, never blank). Unparsed-string rendering forfeits all of it — entity validation (Ch.2/4 Spring) pays off in UI trust.

blocks.title: Reduce the stream
blocks.note: Run it: partial accumulates across tokens, unknown future-frames ignored without harm, done commits the entity. Forward tolerance proven: v1 clients survive v2 servers frame by frame.

items: Typed frame states (streaming/citations/error/complete) with unknown-frame tolerance
Last-Event-ID resume preserves partials; optimistic sends reconcile with server truth
Citations render from validated entities; abstention states designed, never blank

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice reducer and confirm accumulation + tolerance + commit. (b) Add a citations frame mid-stream and verify attachment without disturbing partials. (c) Write the reconnect test (drop after 2 tokens → resume → identical final state) as assertions.
hints: Baseline: 'Hello world' accumulated, future-frame tolerated, phase complete with entity.
Citations attach orthogonally (separate state key): partials accumulate, citations attach, neither disturbs the other.
Reconnect test: frames[0..1] → drop → resume-from-ID → remaining frames → final equals uninterrupted run (resume proof).
exercise.why: Accumulation (streaming), tolerance (versioning), orthogonal attachment (citations), and resume equality (drops) are the four streaming-UI judgments — each asserted, with forward-compat proven.
exercise.code: // Stream-test pattern: accumulate, tolerate unknowns, resume-equal.

quiz.q: Stream drops mid-reply on mobile. Correct UX?
options: Last-Event-ID resume preserving partials: drops become pauses, duplicates deduped by ID
quiz.explain: Resume-everywhere discipline: reconnect from marks, preserve rendered partials, dedupe by ID. Restart-from-zero wastes and frustrates.

quiz.q: Unknown future frame arrives in an old client. Behavior?
options: Ignore by default-case tolerance: v1 clients survive v2 servers frame by frame (forward compatibility by contract)
quiz.explain: Default-case tolerance is version strategy in code: unknown frames skipped, known processing continues. Contracts make it safe.

quiz.q: Optimistic send vs server truth conflict. Resolution?
options: Reconcile: server truth wins with reason shown; optimistic states marked pending until confirmed
quiz.explain: Optimism is provisional by design: pending flags mark unconfirmed states, server responses confirm or roll back with reasons shown.

summary: Typed frame states, resume-preserving partials, entity-rendered citations, reconciled optimism. UI states are product truth — tested like backend contracts.
next: Face delightful — now persistence: threads, messages, and checkpoints owned per user. Next: memory that survives restarts.
